## run() function

Reads the requested providers for the base rows along the declared routes. Rejects with a `DefinitionError` before reading anything when the routes cannot run, with the signal's reason when `options.signal` aborts, and with what failed the run when a load throws what rejects it. `options.ctx` is checked against the graph's `Ctx` (`NoInfer`<!-- -->: the graph alone says what it is), and may be left out when that admits `undefined`<!-- -->. A provider with no route from one of the base rows' entities does not compile, when those are literals (`RoutedProviders`<!-- -->). A run given no `cache` keeps nothing, the scopes of its gates included, so an approval covers its own gate id only: a resume whose keys come in parts (some loaded meanwhile by another call) stops at a gate of its own. A runner given no cache keeps those scopes (`createRunner`<!-- -->); else give a cache. A runner (`createRunner`<!-- -->) gives the options that hold for the process once.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare function run<Meta, Ctx, R extends AnyRoute, const Ps extends readonly ProviderRef[] = readonly string[], const Rs extends readonly BaseRef[] = readonly BaseRef[]>(graph: Graph<Entities, Ctx, Meta, R>, options: RunOptions<NoInfer<Ctx>, Ps, Rs> & NoInfer<{
    readonly providers: RoutedProviders<Ps, R, Rs[number]["entity"]>;
}>): Promise<RunResult<Ps>>;
```
